chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The dower is whatever the two parties agree upon, whether little or much, so this is the dower.

key_terms.الصَّدَاقُ: The dower or bride-price given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What determines the amount of the dower in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the flexibility of the dower (mahr) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that mutual consent (tarāḍin) between the spouses is the primary determinant rather than a fixed statutory amount. It reflects the practical application of Quranic principles, allowing for both nominal and substantial dowers based on the couple's agreement, thereby facilitating marriage accessibility. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the essence of mahr lies in the contractual agreement rather than rigid quantification.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The dower is whatever both are agreed upon, from little or more, so this is the dower’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The amount of mahr (dower) is what people agree upon which can be little or a great deal, that is mahr (dower).”’
